title: Adaptive workload tiler and deterministic golden seeds for CI perf gates
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current benchmark harness relies on a fixed set of golden traces and ad-hoc mixes that drift over time, making CI perf gates brittle. This ticket delivers two coordinated capabilities: (1) an adaptive workload tiler that programmatically composes microprofiles into stable, representative mixes (including adversarial tiles for stress testing), and (2) a deterministic golden-seed generator that produces reproducible seeds and sequence permutations so golden runs are bit-comparable across CI, local dev, and dedicated golden runners.

Goals:
- Produce a tiler library that encodes weighting, temporal correlation, and KV-prefill ratios so we can generate per-model and per-slo workload suites automatically.
- Provide a seed manifest format (seed id, RNG state, input-order map) and tooling to rehydrate exact request sequences inside the harness and the runtime test runners.
- Integrate with CI perf gates to allow dynamic thresholds based on rolling baselines, and a secondary deterministic comparison for regression triage.
- Expose enough telemetry to trace which tile/seed combination caused a regression and attach to PR checks.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Determinism vs realism: seeded deterministic runs will be used for CI golden checks and regression repros; randomized adversarial tiling will be used in nightly stress jobs. This balances deterministic failure repros with coverage of corner cases.
- Storage of seeds: keep manifest in the benchmark repo as small JSON files keyed by model+commit to avoid large binary artifacts in CI.
- Thresholding: use a two-tier gate: an absolute quantile-based gate (P99 increase > X ms) for fast-blocking, and a rolling Z-score gate for noisy but persistent regressions (alerts to perf-alert channel).

Implementation plan:
1) Implement tiler library (go/python hybrid) that reads microprofile fragments and outputs request sequences with metadata (seed-id, tile-id, weight).
2) Seed manifest spec and rehydration CLI (benchctl seed apply --manifest MANIFEST).
3) CI integration: add a golden-run job that runs deterministic seed manifests under a pinned runtime container; post results to perf-dashboard and fail PR if gate violated.
4) Nightly adversarial tiling runs and long-tail telemetry capture for ML-driven tile prioritization next quarter.

Success criteria:
- CI golden-run completes within 30m and disqualifies PRs with >5% P99 regression vs pinned baseline.
- Reproducibility: given a seed-id and the pinned model+container, engineers can reproduce a failing sequence locally.
- Reduced false positive rate for perf gates by 40% in first month after rollout.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: internal alpha with runtime-team only (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: opt-in for model-onboarding pipelines and a subset of active repos (3 weeks).
- Phase 3: opt-out enforcement for all PRs touching runtime-critical code (1 week), then GA.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Seed manifests become large as we add models. Mitigation: hierarchical manifests and tile reuse to keep disk / checkout small.
- Risk: CI runtime variance (cloud noisy neighbors) pollutes deterministic runs. Mitigation: run golden CI on reserved dedicated capacity or Docker-in-Docker pinned containers with CPU/GPU isolation.

Related work: ties to ENG-42109 (meta-benchmark scheduler) for orchestration and ENG-15421 for hybrid prefill profiles.
